title: Anonymous translation remains separate from model history
summary: Translating the model's reasoning for display is an optional bundle with an explicitly chosen provider (Bing by default, or Google) and no fallback. Translated text never replaces stored assistant output and never enters model input.
firstReason: Enabling the bundle is consent to send reasoning text to the chosen service, so a failure must not pick another receiver. Keeping translation outside model history is a correctness rule. The display wrapper is rendered by the host (DH-ADR-3).

title: Paid native Flash translation uses independent queries
summary: Paid reasoning translation is an explicit alternative that uses only the built-in DeepSeek routes and the exact `deepseek-flash` model. Each fragment is one fresh text-only request with no conversation history, and the exact request is recorded in the session before it is sent.
firstReason: Routing through an arbitrary configured model would hide who is billed and who receives the text. Recording the request before dispatch makes the charge auditable. Both rules are independent of the runtime.

title: Machine translation results use shared Session records
summary: Translation requests and results are stored as plugin records in the session they belong to. The request is durable before dispatch and the result before it is shown; a result is reused only for the same provider, language and recipe.
firstReason: A display-only cache repeats external requests, and charges, after a restart. Storing them as ignorable plugin records keeps them out of model history. The Go session log needs the same kind of plugin record.

title: Preserve Web and Desktop plugin identities across experimental consolidation
summary: When packages moved into the experimental directory they kept their published npm names and their existing configuration row ids, enforced by a typed name map, so that installed Web and Desktop profiles kept working.
firstReason: The Go design has no published npm names and no installed upstream profiles to keep working, and it is not required to load them. Inference: the lesson behind the note is to give each Go component an identifier that does not encode its maturity tier, so that promoting it later needs no rename.

title: Pi extensions bridge
summary: Proposal, not built upstream: an experimental bridge that loads unmodified Pi coding-agent extension sources (TypeScript factories) into the host process and serves Pi's extension API from existing extension points, as a capability demonstration.
firstReason: Do not adopt. The bridge depends on importing TypeScript into the host process with the host's full authority and on in-process hooks, which DH-ADR-4 rules out. A Node side process could host such extensions over the plugin protocol, but upstream has not built the bridge and nothing in the Go design depends on it.

title: Pi plugins compatibility — levels of support
summary: Proposal that recommends building nothing now: Pi's newer plugin mechanism is unpublished and unstable, so compatibility is described as six levels, each tied to an upstream trigger, and the product stays at level 0 (no support).
firstReason: The decision to build nothing holds in Go, and more strongly: every higher level runs a JavaScript composition runtime in or beside the host, which DH-ADR-4 would turn into a separate process. Nothing is carried over except the watch on Pi's release status.
